# Scalar and Vector

Scalar and Vector wrappers both expose native R values through RObjC objects.
The key difference is cardinality: a scalar wraps one value, while a vector
wraps an atomic R vector. Neither is a list of RObjC element objects; use an
`RSArray` for an ordered collection of objects.

| Wrapper | Input | Accessor | Missing values |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `RSScalar` subclasses | One R value | `value()` | Shared typed `Class$na` |
| `RSVector` / `RSMutableVector` | An atomic R vector | `asVector()` | NA may occur within the vector |

## Scalar: one typed value

Use `RSScalar_withValue()` to choose a scalar class from a native R value, or
a type-specific constructor such as `RSNumber_withValue()` when the expected
type is known. A missing value returns the corresponding shared NA object;
R `NULL` returns `RSNull$null`.

```{r}
library(robjc)

scalar <- RSScalar_withValue(3L)
stopifnot(scalar$isMemberOf(RSNumber))
stopifnot(identical(scalar$value(), 3L))
stopifnot(identical(RSScalar_withValue(NA_integer_), RSNumber$na))
stopifnot(identical(RSScalar_withValue(NULL), RSNull$null))
```

For the constructor choices, typed NA classes, and date-time time zones, see
`vignette("robjc_scalar_values", package = "robjc")`.

## Vector: multiple native values

`RSVector` is read-only; `RSMutableVector` supports appending, inserting,
replacing, and removing values. Both accept an atomic vector without
dimensions. Values supplied later must match the stored vector's R type and
class. Vector values can contain NA without a separate NA Vector class.

```{r}
vector <- RSVector$new(c(1L, NA_integer_, 3L))
stopifnot(identical(vector$asVector(), c(1L, NA_integer_, 3L)))
stopifnot(is.na(vector$valueAtIndex(2L)))

editable <- vector$mutableCopy()
editable$appendValues(4L)
stopifnot(identical(vector$count(), 3L))
stopifnot(identical(editable$asVector(), c(1L, NA_integer_, 3L, 4L)))
```

Vector indices are one-based. Numeric indices are converted with
`as.integer()` before bounds checks, so `2.9` selects position `2`. Search
methods such as `containsValues()` and `indicesOfValues()` operate on native
values, not wrapped scalar objects.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(editable$valueAtIndex(2.9), NA_integer_))
stopifnot(identical(editable$indicesOfValues(c(3L, 9L)), c(3L, NA_integer_)))
```
